family.shared_definition: an oral presentation delivered to an audience to inform or instruct
family.neutral_stem: Students gathered in the hall for
family.semantic_notes: 'Talk' is more informal and conversational, while 'lecture' typically implies an academic, instructional, or stern delivery.

Nobody was looking forward to the afternoon session, as the presenter was notorious for being dull and monotone. The room slowly filled with unenthusiastic attendees.
The schedule listed a routine update that promised very little excitement. People quietly took their seats, expecting a rather dry and monotonous address.
Word had spread that the presenter's delivery was dry and utterly devoid of passion. Many participants brought coffee just to stay awake.

A short, ten-minute academic presentation was scheduled before the main seminar began. The syllabus noted that the instructor would keep remarks as succinct as possible.
The guest scholar was given a strict five-minute window to introduce the theoretical framework. Attendees quickly found seats to ensure things started without delay.

constructions.semantic_audit_notes: All four combinations ('tedious talk', 'tedious lecture', 'brief talk', 'brief lecture') are fully compatible and natural across all source and target contexts. Source contexts induce a preference for boring or monotonous delivery while leaning informal, whereas target contexts highlight strict time limits and concise academic summaries.
